from setuptools import setup, find_packages

setup(
    name="files-context-agriculture",
    version="0.1.0",
    description="Meltano Cloud industry context for agriculture: datasets for AI assistants and analysts.",
    packages=find_packages(),
    # bundle/ is copied verbatim into the workspace repository; ship every file under it
    include_package_data=True,
)

version: datasets/v0.3
title: "Agriculture: data model"
questions: What are the core entities of agriculture data, and at what grain should each be modelled?
description: |
  The entities most agriculture data reduces to, with the grain and key of each. Use it to map raw
  source tables onto a consistent model. Names are suggestions; keep the organisation's own terms
  where they already exist.

  | Entity | Grain (one row per…) | Notes |
  |---|---|---|
  | `farm` (holding) | holding | Has an official holding number (a County Parish Holding, CPH, in Great Britain) and a business owner |
  | `field` (land parcel) | field version | Boundary geometry, area and official parcel ID. Version it: fields are split, merged and re-measured |
  | `season` | harvest year | The crop year a crop is reported in, usually named for the year of harvest |
  | `crop_plan` (cropping) | field per season per crop | The crop and variety grown, sown area, previous crop. Catch and cover crops are extra rows |
  | `operation` (field activity) | operation on a field | Drilling, spraying, fertilising, cultivation, harvest. Date, machine, operator, area worked |
  | `input_application` | product applied in an operation | Product, rate per hectare, total quantity, unit. Sprays carry the product's registration number |
  | `harvest` (yield record) | field per season per crop | Tonnes harvested, moisture, area harvested. Yield maps sit beneath it at point or grid grain |
  | `soil_sample` | sample | Location, date, pH, P, K, Mg indices, organic matter |
  | `animal` | individual animal | Official ear tag or ID, species, breed, sex, date of birth, dam. Poultry and pigs are usually managed as `batch` instead |
  | `animal_movement` | movement | From and to holdings, date, reason. Reported to the official register within a deadline |
  | `animal_event` | event | Weighing, treatment, service, calving, death. Treatments carry the medicine, dose and withdrawal period |
  | `milk_record` | animal per milking or test day | Volume, butterfat, protein, somatic cell count |
  | `grain_contract` | contract | Buyer, crop, tonnage, price basis, delivery window, quality specification |
  | `intake_ticket` (delivery) | load delivered | Weighbridge gross and net weights, moisture, quality tests, deductions |

  ## Relationships

  - A **farm** has many **fields**; a field has one **crop plan** per crop per **season**.
  - A crop plan has many **operations**, and each operation applies zero or more **inputs**.
  - A crop plan ends in a **harvest**, delivered as **intake tickets** against **grain contracts**.
  - An **animal** belongs to one holding at a time; **movements** change the holding and **events**
    record what happens to it.

  ## Status and history

  Field boundaries, crop plans and contracts change during the season, and animals move between
  holdings. Keep the history of field versions and animal locations, so a report can be run "as at"
  a date and a season's figures still use that season's field areas.

  #agriculture #organisation-context

version: datasets/v0.3
title: "Agriculture: modelling it in dbt"
questions: How should raw agriculture data be modelled in dbt so that it reconciles?
description: |
  Conventions for building dbt models on raw agriculture data. They apply on top of the workspace's
  usual dbt layout: staging, then intermediate, then marts.

  ## Seasons and dates

  - **Model a season dimension** (`dim_season`) and give every crop record a `harvest_year`. Do not
    derive the season from the calendar year of an operation: autumn-drilled crops are sown in the
    year before they are harvested.
  - Keep the **financial year** separate from the harvest year, and map costs to both. A spray bought
    in one financial year can be applied to the next season's crop.
  - Livestock data runs on dates, not seasons: use event dates, and the animal's age at the event.

  ## Units and quantities

  - **Normalise units in staging.** Convert areas to hectares, weights to tonnes or kilograms, and
    volumes to litres, and name each column for its unit (`area_ha`, `net_weight_t`).
  - **Standardise moisture.** Yields and intake weights are reported at different moisture contents.
    Keep the measured weight and moisture, and add a weight at the standard moisture for the crop.
  - **Product rates need the product.** Convert application rates to active ingredient or nutrient
    (kg N, P₂O₅, K₂O per hectare) with a product table, rather than summing litres of different
    products.

  ## Fields and space

  - Treat **fields as slowly changing**. Snapshot field boundaries and areas, and join crop records to
    the field version valid in that season, so past yields keep their original area.
  - Keep geometry in the warehouse's spatial type (or WKT/GeoJSON text where there is none), and the
    area as a separate number: recalculating area from geometry differs by projection.
  - Yield and as-applied maps are large point data. Aggregate them to field or grid-cell grain in an
    intermediate model; do not join raw points into marts.

  ## Livestock

  - Use the **official animal ID** as the key, and keep management tags or names as attributes.
  - Build **animal location history** from movements, and a daily animals-on-hand table from it:
    mortality, stocking rates and feed per head all divide by it.
  - Reconcile births, deaths and movements against the official register (BCMS in Great Britain).

  ## Tests

  Add these beside the usual `unique` and `not_null` tests:

  - **Area:** cropped area per field and season does not exceed the field's area (except for catch or
    double crops, flagged explicitly).
  - **Yield range:** yield per hectare falls within a plausible range for the crop; flag outliers,
    which are usually unit or area errors.
  - **Stock balance:** opening stock + intake − dispatches = closing stock, within a shrinkage
    tolerance.
  - **Animal balance:** opening head count + births + moves on − deaths − moves off = closing count.
  - **Accepted values** on crop codes, operation types and species.
  - **Freshness** on telematics and sensor sources, which stop silently when a device loses signal.

  ## Naming

  - Prefix models by layer (`stg_`, `int_`, `fct_`, `dim_`), and name facts for their grain:
    `fct_field_operations`, `fct_harvests`, `fct_animal_events`, `fct_animals_on_hand_daily`.

  ## Sensitive columns

  Tag personal columns (owners, staff, contractors) and commercially sensitive ones (prices,
  contract terms) in the model YAML, for example `meta: {pii: true}`. See *Agriculture: handling the
  data*.

  #agriculture #organisation-context

# files-context-agriculture

A Meltano [file bundle](https://docs.meltano.com/concepts/plugins/#file-bundles) of **industry
context for agriculture**. Meltano Cloud adds it to a workspace whose organisation's industry
is Agriculture.

The bundle holds datasets with no query. Each one is a written briefing: the segments and source
systems of the industry, its core entities, the metrics it runs on, how to model its data in dbt,
and how to handle its data. They are written for an AI assistant (or an analyst) working in the
workspace, for example one building dbt models on raw agriculture data.

```
analyze/datasets/agriculture/
  overview.yml
  data-model.yml
  metrics.yml
  dbt-modelling.yml
  data-handling.yml
```

## Organisation knowledge: `#organisation-context`

Every dataset here is tagged `#organisation-context`, the tag of an organisation's knowledge in Meltano
Cloud. The `get_organisation_knowledge` MCP tool returns the full text of every dataset with it, for an
AI assistant to read before it models, transforms or queries the workspace's data. In the repository,
`grep -rl '#organisation-context' analyze/datasets` finds the same set. Tag a dataset of your own the
same way to add it.

## Install

Meltano Cloud installs it when Agriculture is chosen as the workspace's industry, in the
setup wizard or with the `set_organisation_context` MCP tool.

In a Meltano project of your own, save this definition to a file outside the project, for example
`/tmp/files-context-agriculture.yml`:

```yaml
name: files-context-agriculture
namespace: files_context_agriculture
variant: matatika
pip_url: git+https://github.com/meltano/files-context-agriculture.git@v0.1.0
update:
  '*.yml': true
```

then add the bundle from the project directory. `meltano add` writes the datasets; a plain
`meltano install` does not:

```sh
meltano add --plugin-type files files-context-agriculture --from-ref /tmp/files-context-agriculture.yml
```

`update: '*.yml': true` lets `meltano upgrade files` refresh the datasets from a newer version.

## Release

Tag a version (`git tag -a v0.1.0 -m v0.1.0 && git push --tags`) and bump the `pip_url` ref in the
Meltano Cloud registry definition (`plugins/files/files-context-agriculture--matatika.yml`).

These datasets are general industry context, not legal, regulatory, agronomic or veterinary advice.

version: datasets/v0.3
title: "Agriculture: handling the data"
questions: What care does agriculture data need in the warehouse?
description: |
  Agriculture data mixes personal data about farmers and workers, commercially sensitive data, and
  records the law requires a farm to keep. These are general practices for a warehouse holding it.
  They are not legal or compliance advice: the organisation decides what applies to it.

  ## Classify the data

  | Class | Examples | Handling |
  |---|---|---|
  | Personal data | Farmer and landowner names, addresses, phone numbers, holding owner details | Restrict access, mask in non-production and in marts that do not need it. A sole trader's farm business data is also personal data |
  | Worker data | Seasonal worker identity, right-to-work and visa details, accommodation, pay | Restrict to HR and payroll roles. Do not load identity documents |
  | Location data | Field boundaries, GPS tracks, machine positions, farmyard locations | Treat as sensitive: it identifies people and premises, and helps theft of machinery and livestock |
  | Commercial data | Yields, prices, contract terms, input costs, margins | Restrict to the roles that need it. Aggregate before sharing across farms or with partners |
  | Statutory records | Animal IDs and movements, medicine records, pesticide applications, fertiliser records | Keep complete and unaltered. Never delete or overwrite them in the warehouse |

  ## Practices

  - **Least privilege.** Separate raw, staging and mart schemas, and grant raw schemas only to the
    pipelines and the people who maintain them.
  - **Keep statutory records whole.** Load animal, medicine and spray records append-only, keep the
    original record and its load time, and model corrections as new rows.
  - **Shared and pooled data.** Benchmarking groups, co-operatives and agronomists often see many
    farms' data. Agree who owns each farm's data and what can be shared, and share only aggregates
    unless each farm agrees otherwise.
  - **Retention.** Some farm records must be kept for a minimum period (for example, veterinary
    medicine records and pesticide application records). Agree retention with the organisation, and
    keep personal data no longer than needed.
  - **Data subject requests.** Under GDPR and UK GDPR a farmer or worker can ask for their data or for
    its erasure, so know where each person's data lives.

  ## Rules and codes to be aware of

  Which apply depends on the organisation's country and activities. Common ones:

  - **UK:** UK GDPR; cattle, sheep, goat and pig identification and movement reporting (BCMS, ARAMS
    and eAML2 in England); veterinary medicine record keeping; pesticide application records; the
    Farming Rules for Water and nitrate vulnerable zone (NVZ) rules in England; assurance schemes
    such as Red Tractor.
  - **EU:** GDPR, the Common Agricultural Policy's land parcel identification system and claims, and
    animal identification and traceability rules.
  - **US:** USDA programmes and their reporting, and state privacy laws.
  - **Agricultural data codes:** the EU Code of Conduct on agricultural data sharing and similar
    industry codes set expectations on who controls farm data.

  #agriculture #organisation-context

version: datasets/v0.3
title: "Agriculture: key metrics"
questions: Which metrics does an agriculture organisation run on, and how is each calculated?
description: |
  Standard definitions of the metrics agriculture organisations report. Confirm each one with the
  farm manager, agronomist or finance team before building it: organisations differ on which area
  they divide by, which costs they allocate, and which season a figure belongs to.

  ## Crops

  | Metric | Definition |
  |---|---|
  | Yield | Tonnes harvested ÷ hectares harvested, at a standard moisture (for example 15% for wheat). Say which area: cropped or harvested |
  | Yield vs five-year average | Season's yield ÷ mean yield of the same crop over the previous five seasons |
  | Input use per hectare | Quantity of a product (kg of nitrogen, litres of a spray) ÷ hectares treated |
  | Nitrogen use efficiency | Nitrogen removed in the harvested crop ÷ nitrogen applied |
  | Variable cost per hectare | Seed, fertiliser, sprays and other direct inputs for a crop ÷ cropped hectares |
  | Gross margin per hectare | (Output value − variable costs) ÷ cropped hectares. Output value includes the crop and any by-product such as straw |
  | Cost of production per tonne | (Variable costs + allocated fixed costs) ÷ tonnes produced. State how fixed costs were allocated |

  ## Livestock

  | Metric | Definition |
  |---|---|
  | Daily liveweight gain (DLWG) | (Weight at second weighing − weight at first) ÷ days between them |
  | Feed conversion ratio (FCR) | Feed consumed ÷ liveweight gained, over the same period and group |
  | Mortality rate | Animal deaths in the period ÷ average number of animals on hand |
  | Calving interval | Days between successive calvings of the same cow, averaged over the herd |
  | Milk yield per cow | Litres sold or produced ÷ average number of cows in milk, or of all cows. Say which |
  | Somatic cell count (SCC) | Bulk tank or individual cell count, in thousands of cells per ml. A measure of udder health and milk quality |
  | Antibiotic use | Milligrams of active ingredient per population correction unit (mg/PCU), as used in UK sector reporting |

  ## Trading and supply

  | Metric | Definition |
  |---|---|
  | Contract coverage | Tonnes contracted ÷ tonnes expected to be harvested or in store |
  | Average achieved price | Value of sales ÷ tonnes sold, after quality deductions and haulage |
  | Intake rejection rate | Loads rejected ÷ loads delivered |
  | Stock in store | Opening stock + intake − dispatches − shrinkage (drying and handling losses) |

  ## Farm business

  | Metric | Definition |
  |---|---|
  | Farm business income | Output less costs, before the owner's own labour and capital are paid for. Follows the UK Farm Business Survey definition where used |
  | Return on capital employed (ROCE) | Profit before interest and tax ÷ capital employed |
  | Share of income from subsidies and schemes | Scheme and subsidy payments ÷ total farm income |

  #agriculture #organisation-context

version: datasets/v0.3
title: "Agriculture: industry overview"
questions: What does an agriculture organisation's data look like, and where does it come from?
description: |
  Industry context for this workspace, for the people and AI assistants working in it. It has no
  query: it is a briefing to read before modelling or analysing this organisation's data.

  ## Segments

  Agriculture covers organisations that grow crops, raise livestock, or supply and buy from the
  people who do. The segments differ in which entities and metrics matter most:

  - **Arable and horticulture:** cereals, oilseeds, vegetables, fruit and protected crops. Fields,
    crop plans, inputs applied, operations and yields drive the data.
  - **Livestock and dairy:** beef, sheep, pigs, poultry and dairy herds. Individual animals or
    batches, movements, feed, health treatments, milk recording and weights drive the data.
  - **Agribusiness and input supply:** seed, fertiliser, crop protection, feed and machinery
    dealers. Orders, product registrations, grower accounts and seasonal sales drive the data.
  - **Grain trading, storage and processing:** merchants, co-operatives, mills and packers.
    Contracts, intake tickets, quality tests, stock in store and movements drive the data.
  - **Agronomy and ag-tech:** advisory services, precision farming and remote sensing. Field
    boundaries, soil samples, recommendations, imagery and sensor readings drive the data.
  - **Estates and mixed farms:** often all of the above, plus land, subsidies and environmental
    schemes.

  ## Typical source systems

  | System | Examples | What it holds |
  |---|---|---|
  | Farm management (FMIS) | Gatekeeper, Muddy Boots, Farmplan, Climate FieldView, John Deere Operations Center, Trimble Ag Software | Fields, crop plans, operations, inputs applied, yields |
  | Machinery telematics | John Deere Operations Center, CLAAS Telematics, AgLeader, ISOBUS task files | Machine passes, as-applied and yield maps, fuel, hours |
  | Livestock management | Herdwatch, Farmplan Cattle Manager, the herd's milk-recording service | Animals, movements, breeding, treatments, weights |
  | Milking and parlour | Lely, DeLaval, GEA | Yields per milking, conductivity, robot visits |
  | Government registers | BCMS (UK cattle), ARAMS (UK sheep and goats), the Rural Payments service | Official animal records, movements, scheme claims |
  | Accounting / ERP | Xero, Sage, Farmplan Business Manager, Microsoft Dynamics 365, SAP | General ledger, invoices, costs, payroll |
  | Grain and trading | The merchant's or co-operative's trading and intake system | Contracts, intake tickets, quality, stock |
  | Weather and sensing | Met Office, weather stations, soil moisture probes, satellite imagery (Sentinel-2) | Rainfall, temperature, moisture, vegetation indices |

  ## What makes the data different

  - **It runs on seasons, not calendar years.** A crop is planted in one year and harvested in the
    next, and a harvest year, a financial year and a calendar year rarely line up. Say which one each
    report uses.
  - **It is spatial.** Fields have boundaries, areas and parcel IDs that change when fields are
    split, merged or re-measured. Yield and application data come as maps, not single numbers.
  - **Units vary.** Hectares and acres, tonnes and bushels, litres and kilograms of product, and yields
    at different moisture contents. Normalise before comparing.
  - **Biology adds noise.** Weather, disease and soil make year-on-year comparisons hard: compare
    against a multi-year average, not one year.
  - **Some data is regulated.** Animal identification and movements, pesticide and fertiliser
    records, and subsidy claims have statutory rules. See *Agriculture: handling the data*.

  Related datasets: *data model*, *metrics*, *modelling it in dbt*, *handling the data*.

  #agriculture #organisation-context
